findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment:
2-102.12(A)
No Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) was present at the facility during today’s inspection. The presence of a CFPM helps to ensure safe food handling practices, and decreases the risk of Foodborne illnesses by overseeing facilities and educating food handlers. Ensure there is a CFPM present at the facility any time food is being served.

Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 
Inspectors observed working chemical container (spray bottle) in the kitchen without a label. CORRECTED: PIC was informed, and the spray bottle was labeled as “Disinfectant”. Make sure every chemical working bottle is clearly labeled with a common name for preventing misuse.

Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 
Inspectors observed the following non food contact surfaces that have an accumulation of soil residues.
1. The milk cooler with the chocolate milk has a spill in the bottom that is giving off an odor.
2. The milk cooler with the 1% milk has ice accumulation on the sides.
3. The standing freezer has residues hanging from the top of the ceiling.
4. The standing cooler has residues accumulating on the bottom.
5. The coffee maker grounds basket underside has residue buildup.
PIC was notified, and these areas will be cleaned. Ensure that all nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned frequently to prevent an accumulation of soils.

Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: No Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) was present at the facility during today’s inspection. The presence of a CFPM helps to ensure safe food handling practices, and decreases the risk of Food borne illnesses by overseeing facilities and educating food handlers. Ensure there is a CFPM present at the facility any time food is being served.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: Signed employee reporting agreements were not available upon request. CORRECTED- the inspector provided the person in charge (PIC) with SCDPH employee health reporting agreements. A spot check will occur on 09/19/25 to check that the PIC has signed forms from the facilities volunteers.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no sanitizer available at the start of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- the inspector demonstrated how to prepare the sanitizer compartment of the triple sink- per the label’s instructions. Sanitizer was observed at 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer is available for food contact surfaces on days where food assembly is required (i.e.- Taco Tuesdays where volunteers assemble tacos).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
There is ponding water/spilled milk in the left milk cooler. Clean and maintain clean the insides of coolers.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Volunteer was observed washing hands without proper technique. The manual faucet was shut off without a barrier. CORRECTED- Proper handwashing was discussed, and volunteer re-washed hands prior to continuing with food handling.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Dish machine observed with a maximum final rinse plate temperature of 143F. Ensure the sanitizing rinse of the dish machine reaches at least 160F on surfaces (dishes or dish temperature sticker) or 180F at the manifold. See General Comments for additional information.
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 160F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. [Pf]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12 Volunteer was observed washing hands without proper technique. Hands were washed for a few seconds, and the manual faucet was shut off without a barrier. Proper handwashing was discussed, and volunteer re-washed hands prior to continuing with food handling. Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of a forearm or elbow is also acceptable for shutting of the handwashing sink.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Volunteer began to put on gloves without first washing their hands. Proper handwashing prior to glove use was discussed. Hands were washed prior to putting on gloves to continue with food handling.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed upon entering the kitchen, prior to putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle in the kitchen labeled as Buckeye Neutral (quat disinfectant) contained a different germicidal cleaner. Another spray bottle labeled as Buckeye Neutral and contained quat solution was a darker green color than the germicidal cleaner. Proper labeling of spray bottles was discussed. Head of maintenance will order additional labels for products. Chemical was labeled using a piece of paper taped on the bottle until labels are received from the company.   
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 The person who is now in charge of food service at the school completed an online food handler course but does not have a food manager certification. PIC was provided information about food manager courses, including options for online courses.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Volunteers were observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing was discussed with the lead volunteer for the day. PIC was given signage to post at the handsink that specifies the use of a barrier to shut off the faucet once handwashing is completed. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of a forearm or elbow is also acceptable for shutting of the handwashing sink.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle labeled Neutral Germicidal Cleaner contained Buckeye Neutral quat solution. A proper label was provided during the inspection.   
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site, such as bleach solution, shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13 Facility does not have a way to measure the surface temperature at the dish rack during the final rinse of a ware washing cycle. Dishwasher temperature test strips were ordered. 
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature. Surface temperature at dishes upon completion of final rinse must be at least 160F for proper heat sanitization.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-502.11 The wash gauge was slowly moving and reading at ~130F after a half dozen cycles. The rinse gauge was reading between 180F and 190F, and it took 6 full cycles for the surface temperature at the dishes to reach 160F. Head of maintenance will call for service. (see general comments for details)
Water temperature measuring devices shall be maintained in good repair and be accurate within the intended range of use.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12 Volunteers were observed washing hands without proper technique. One person washed hands briefly for less that 20 seconds. Another person shut off the manual faucet prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing was discussed, and a sign explaining proper technique is posted above the handsink. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of a forearm or elbow is also acceptable for shutting of the handwashing sink.

2-301.14 Volunteer did not wash hands at the designated handsink prior to putting on gloves. 
One volunteer was handling money and putting on gloves without handwashing in the same area to handle unwrapped deli sandwiches. Handwashing between tasks was discussed.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must be washed before putting on gloves/between glove changes and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands, such as handling money.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 One volunteer was observed washing hands at the 2 part sink, and another volunteer with gloved hands stated she washed her hands at the 2 part sink prior to inspector's arrival. Proper handwashing at the designated hadnsink only was discussed. Volunteers were later observed washing hands at the handsink. 
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 Volunteer was not wearing gloves while bagging popcorn. Popcorn was spilling over his hands during the process back into the bottom of the popcorn machine with remaining product. Glove use was discussed, and gloves were put on prior to bagging more popcorn. 
Food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11 Single use gloves were observed out of the original packaging on a table in the cafeteria. Keep single use gloves in their original package until they are needed for use to protect gloves from potential contamination. 
Single service and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.
findings.citation_text:
4-904.11 Plastic utensils were observed in containers with food contact surfaces and handles all facing multiple directions. Children get their own utensils, and the current storage practice allows for food contact surfaces to be touched by multiple hands. Store utensils all facing one direction so only the handles are touched. 
Single use utensils shall be stored and handled so that contamination of food- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 Volunteers were observed wearing the same gloves to touch various surfaces other than prepared, portioned food products and did not change gloves between touching general surfaces and going back to food handling. One volunteer preparing popcorn touched cardboard boxes with gloved hands, and another volunteer handled papers in a binder. A third volunteer used the back of her gloved hand to itch her nose. All persons in the kitchen at the time were advised on proper glove use, including changing gloves between tasks and after touching anything unrelated to food prep/handling. Handwashing prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes was also discussed.
One volunteer working at the money table was also responsible for serving prepared sandwiches with toppings. Tongs were available for handing tomatoes and pickles. However, gloves were worn to handle and slice sandwiches. It appeared the volunteer was preparing to put on the same pair of gloves that were removed and sitting by the pan of sandwiches. Gloves were discarded. Handwashing after handling money and prior to putting on gloves was discussed. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.
NOTE: Best practice is to immediately remove gloves when stepping away from food prep/handling. Discard the gloves that are removed. Get a new pair of gloves after properly washing hands prior to returning to food prep/handling.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13 Facility does not have a way to measure the surface temperature at the dish rack during a ware washing cycle. Options for temperature indicating devices were discussed, including a dishtemp plate simulator and dishwashing temperature test strips. 
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature. Surface temperature at dishes upon completion of final rinse must be at least 160F for proper heat sanitization.

The wash gauge was slowly moving and only reading at 120F after a half dozen full cycles. If the machine was ran several more times the gauge would likely be reading at 150F/above. The rinse gauge was reading between 180F and 190F, and it took multiple cycles for the surface temperature at the dishes to reach 160F. Get the dish machine serviced to verify proper function.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Gehl's cheese sauce machine was observed to not be holding at proper temperature. Built in thermometer was observed around 120°F; a dispensed portion of cheese sauce was temped at 119°F-122°F with inspector's stem thermometer. Staff noted the new dispensers in the kitchen are supposed to be used, and the old Gehl's dispenser is not supposed to have product in it. Staff were advised to remove the unopened portion of cheese sauce from the dispenser and to discard the bag that is currently hooked up to dispense from the Gehl's machine. Remove the Gehl's machine from the food service area and only use the new cheese sauce dispensers.

Hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be maintained at 135°F/above during storage, display and service.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - An old organic apple box was used by Fritz's staff for transport of clean utensils and other items used for food service today. The box had staining and stuck on debris in it. Cook stated the boxes used for transport of such items are replaced frequently, but it was advised to use a cleanable container (e.g. totes with lids, clean bus tub, etc.) and to cease the practice of reusing containers that previously contained raw, unwashed produce. 

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.160, 510, & 512 - Cook was observed adjusting his glasses with gloved hands. Cook was advised on the personal practice of adjusting glasses with gloved hands, and he stated he was not handling food at that time. The cook also noted he planned to wash his hands and put on a new pair of gloves prior to food service. Cook discarded the gloves at the request of inspector. 

Cook was later observed washing hands without proper technique. Cook had bare hand contact with manual faucet to shut off the water prior to obtaining paper towels to dry his hands. Cook was advised to avoid touching the faucet with bare hands once handwashing is done and utilize a barrier to shut off the manual faucet to avoid contaminating freshly washed hands. (Proper handwashing technique sign is posted at the kitchen handsink)

Food service workers shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. Gloves are intended for one use and need to be discarded when soiled, torn, or an interruption in service occurs.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Detergent bottle hooked up at heat sanitizing dish machine was empty. School staff were advised and noted the custodial staff would be made aware immediately to hook up a new bottle of detergent.

Dish machines shall be properly installed and maintained in good repair. Dish machines shall be operated in accordance with the manufacturers instructions. Automatic dispensers and liquid injectors, if any, shall be properly installed and maintained. All equipment and utensils placed in dish machines shall be exposed to all dishwashing cycles.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The base of one of the newer cheese sauce dispensers had a small pile of old, hardened cheese on it beneath the dispenser opening. Clean the general surfaces of the dispensers after each use, and maintain them clean.

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.290 - Ice scoop was observed on top of the ice machine sitting partially on a paper towel and partially in direct contact with the top of the machine. The ice scoop was removed to run through the dish machine. Store the ice scoop in a clean container, and maintain the scoop and holder clean.
NOTE: The ice scoop may be stored in the ice machine as long as the handle is positioned so it is not touching the ice.

Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Facility does not have a chemical test kit for checking the concentration of quaternary ammonia based sanitizer used for wiping down lunch tables (see #41b). Obtain and use a quat test kit for checking the concentration of the solution. 

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The ovens were soiled with general buildup inside. Clean the ovens.

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.850 & 860 - Clean utensils were observed with food contact surfaces extended up out of storage crocks. Store the utensils with handles presented out to avoid touching food contact surfaces when retrieving utensils for use. Maintain storage containers clean.

Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be stored and handled in a way that protects them from contamination. Store cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1280 - Personal belongings (coat and purses) were observed on a cold holding cart in the kitchen. Staff noted the cart in question is utilized during Friday lunch service. Personal belongings need to be stored separate from food prep/service and equipment storage areas. Provide an area for volunteers to store their belongings.

An adequate area must be provided for the storage of belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
7501300 & 1320 - Four improperly labeled spray bottles of a greenish colored liquid were observed in the cafeteria. One bottle had "peroxide concentrate" on it, and another bottle just had "46" on it. . Two bottles had old, peeling labels that indicated they contained a neutral germicidal cleaner. Maintenance worker showed inspector what chemical was actually in the bottles (dispensed from the chemical closet), and it is an ammonia based sanitizer. Maintenance noted they just switched to the product in question recently, and new labels have been ordered for bottles. In the meantime, hand written labels will suffice.
The chemical in use, Buckeye Eco Neutral Disinfectant, is used for wiping down tables between lunch shifts. Maintain the Safety Data Sheet (formerly known as MSDS) for the product. It will have all the necessary information required for staff to use it properly. The label is the law; follow manufacturer's instruction when using.  

Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 510: Observed an employee handle chemical cloth then clean plates that were ready for service to children without washing hands or changing gloves between tasks. Discussed hand washing with cook. Hands were washed. Bare hands were also observed being used to turn off the faucet after handwashing. Discussed using a barrier when touching soiled surfaces.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 120:Observed a box of bananas on the ground by the handsink. Stored off the ground during the inspection.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 880: Observed a sleeve of portion cups stored on the floor. Moved off the floor during the inspection.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment: There are two Gehl's cheese sauce dispensers in the kitchen. These are used for the Sports Boosters. Janice was present and is a representative of the boosters. The Gehl's cheese dispensers were temped and found to be holding at 107-111F. Food was dispensed from the unit into portion cups and probed to determine the temperature. Recommended the destruction of the cheese sauce. Boosters should be able to order/replace the Gehl's dispensers from Gehl's. Even the thermometer on the side of the unit indicated temperatures between 110 and 120F.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800: The underside of the coffee machine (spout) is observed soiled. Clean the coffee machine. Discussed cleaning schedule with Mr. Thronberry.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: Crocks holding utensils were soiled in the bottoms. 750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. Crocks and utensils were run through the dish machine.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment: Chemicals and spices were mixed in the cabinets above the dish sink.  750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.  Chemicals were moved to the cabinet with cleaning cloths and spices were placed together on a shelf in a different cabinet.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F. There are no thermometers in the milk coolers.  The outside gauge is registering 37F and the milk inside is 41F. An independent thermometer would help to identify the issue. Provide independent thermometers for milk coolers.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120 At all times food shall be protected from potential contamination. The food bar for condiments is not protected. Observed students leaning over the food during service.  Provide sneeze guard for salad/food bar. Use of cold holding table which has a sneeze guard built in seems like the natural choice to abate this violation.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Clean serving utensils are stored in a bucket with handles down and food contact surfaces exposed.  Store utensils protected.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment: 750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination. observed purse and cell phones to be on food prep/service locations in the kitchen.  Items were moved from these areas to on top of the cooler, freezer and drink cooler.  Provide more propper location for storage of employee/volunteer personal property that does not intrude on the food service area. Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.comment: 750.600: Observed the re-use of single-use gloves. The worn gloves were removed to be used again, for picking up bagels. Deli tissue or tongs can be used to handle bagels and then gloves would not be necessary, unless you will touch the bagel.
